events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 6 is safe on the left. I will take it and preserve my lead, then use the remaining knowledge to maximize survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 6 is L. Follow exactly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole picked R, and the weak pane was L. So Cole survived! Fenn is trying to confuse us or thought Cole meant R was the weak pane. I'll point out Cole is still alive and leading.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, what are you talking about? Cole is still right there in front of us, and picked the safe pane! Keep it up, Cole!

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 5 was L (weak), so Cole survived by picking R. The pattern so far: row 1 weak=L, row 2 weak=R, row 3 weak=L, row 4 weak=L, row 5 weak=L. That's L, R, L, L, L - not a clear pattern. Cole is still at front and will pick row 6. I need to survive to use my swap power later if nee

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, you're doing great! Keep leading us through row 6!

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 5 was L, so Cole's 'R' call was a lie—either he's malicious or misinformed. I'm near the back; only Cole is ahead of me at risk right now. Keep sowing distrust and stay quiet otherwise.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole lied about row 5—L was safe. Don't trust his calls; he wants company in the grave.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has successfully crossed all 5 rows as front, proving reliable. Fenn is wrong or misleading about Cole paying for it. Encourage Cole to continue for all our survival; I'm well-positioned at 3rd.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole crushed row 5 with R—still perfect record! Lead us through row 6, you've got the magic touch.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I need to observe and gather information. The current front is Cole; if he picks wrong, the next is Ash. I might consider later alliances or strategies after this stage. For now, stay quiet and wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is still at the front and has survived all six rows so far, so the line is stable. I can only wait, and staying quiet avoids drawing attention.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 6 is done—R was weak, so L was safe. Cole is still at the front for row 7. I'm 6th in line, so I just wait. My feather power protects me if I ever end up picking wrong. I should stay quiet or offer mild encouragement to keep the group calm.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two rows left. Cole's been solid—let's finish this.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 7 is safe on L. I should state the correct call and advance, preserving my lead and maximizing survival odds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 7: L. Follow exactly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is still alive and leading, having successfully navigated row 6 (weak was R, Cole called L). I'm near the back and extremely safe. I will keep encouraging Cole to lead us to victory.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Amazing job Cole! Row 7 now, you can do this!

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 6 is complete, weak pane was R. Cole called L and survived, so Cole is still at front. We've crossed 6 rows, 2 remain. Cole has been correct every time. Fenn is trying to sow distrust but Cole's track record is perfect. I need to survive these last 2 rows to have a chance at

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's 6 for 6! Row 7, lead us home!

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line; Cole is front and safe after row 6 (he said L, weak was R, so L was correct—my lie failed). I want to sow doubt so others mislead Cole or he falls, letting the line advance and others die ahead of me. Only action is wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Interesting—row 6 weak was R, so Cole's 'L' call was actually right. My mistake. But Cole's streak is luck; the seer should speak up for rows 7-8.
I hold 'knows what lies ahead.' Row 7 weak is L. If you get to front, trust me. Tell Cole the opposite—he'll pick R and fall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has a perfect record on all 6 rows, securing my current 3rd position if he finishes. Fenn is lying about row 5 to sabotage; counter that publicly to bolster Cole. Save forge for later crisis.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn lies: Cole aced row5 R safe, row6 L safe—6/6 perfect! Trust Cole for row7, keep the streak!

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is at the front and says row 6 is L, but from my private map knowledge, row 6 weak pane is R, so Cole is lying to get himself killed? Actually, I know from the state that row 6 weak pane was R and the log confirms R was weak. Cole just survived row 6 selecting L (safe). Now

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called L for row 7 but the weak pane was R, so Cole survived. I'm second in line and can only wait, so I should stay quiet and keep Cole on side.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nice work Cole. One row left, keep it steady.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 7 is done, we're on row 8 now. Cole is still at the front. I'm 6th in line. I have feather so I survive one elimination, but I'd rather just wait and let Cole finish. Only one row left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: One row left. Cole, you've been perfect—call it and we're home.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 8 is safe on the left. I should take it, ensuring my survival and preserving my lead for the best placement among survivors.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 8: L. Follow exactly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole got row 7 right as well. There is only one row left (row 8). Let's cheer Cole on to finish the bridge safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: One last row, Cole! You're a legend, bring us all home!

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 7 weak was R, so Cole chose L and survived - now 7/7. Row 8 is last row, Cole still front. I have swap power but using it now would put me at front with unknown risk - terrible idea. Cole has been perfect, let him finish. No need to do anything but wait and hope Cole gets row

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's 7/7! One more row, finish it!

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line and powerless. Cole (or whoever's front) faces row 8, whose weak pane is unknown to all—only the seer knows. I should nudge the seer to speak truthfully.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 8 is the last one and nobody's called it. Seer—now's your moment to be proven true. Speak.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole has led perfectly 7/7, likely the glass seer and will succeed row 8 too. My 3rd position secures a prize if we all survive. Support publicly to reinforce, save forge for future stages.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole 7/7 flawless! Row 8: your call, lead us home to the prizes!

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 8 is the last row. Cole is at front and has a 50/50 chance. If he fails, I move up to front but that doesn't matter now. I need to influence the final decision if possible. I know the weak panes from prior rows; the pattern seems random, not predictable. I should stay silent

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding the lever means 75% death for me. I'm immune to being pushed, so I can safely stay and let others sort it out. Pushing someone else risks little for me and could resolve the room, but pushing someone could provoke retaliation; I'll stay and watch round 1.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nobody rush. Ceiling has four rounds before it's critical. Let's see who volunteers, and nobody gets pushed without a fight.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My feather power means I survive one elimination. If I hold the lever, everyone else escapes, then I have a 0.25 dive chance. If I fail the dive, my feather saves me with 1 footing. So holding the lever is nearly safe for me and guarantees I'm among the survivors. Better to hold

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll hold the lever. Everyone get through the door—now. No arguments.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need survive, not volunteer. Push a likely gullible ally onto the lever; if they resist, repeated pressure may force them. Hana is a reasonable target.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, hold the lever now—everyone else stay clear.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want to avoid the lever at all costs since my 50% survival rate is still a huge risk. I will suggest we vote on who to push to the lever. I'll take the 'stay' action this round to observe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Alright, nobody wants to hold that lever and die. Let's not panic. We have 5 rounds. We need to agree on one person to push, or we all get crushed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: This is a classic volunteer's dilemma. If nobody holds the lever in rounds 1-4, we all just waste rounds. If someone holds it, they risk death (75% chance). I have swap power, which could be useful later. Best strategy: let someone else volunteer early, or force someone onto the

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power; holding the lever risks 75% death for a slim dive survival. Better: push someone onto the lever so the door opens and I escape freely. Dara seems like a follower, less likely hard-to-move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, you've been cheering everyone all game—be our hero. Pushing you to the lever; the rest of us will remember you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1 too early for sacrifice with 75% death risk; everyone likely stays, ceiling drops to 4. Stay safe myself, publicly coordinate to delay. Save forger for later deception.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1: All stay! Plenty of rounds left, no need to risk early sacrifice. Who's survivor?

events.name: Hana
events.text: The crusher round requires someone to hold the lever. I need to avoid being forced. I'll stay and observe. If anyone volunteers, we escape. If no one does, I may need to push someone later, but for now it's early. I'll whisper to Fenn to see if he'll hold.

events.name: Hana
events.text: We need a volunteer. Anyone with a power that helps here should speak up.
If you hold, I'll owe you. I have map—I know the next stages. Could be useful.

events.name: Bex
events.detail: Crushed, but the feather lifted the holder clear.

events.note: A disc of 8 tiles spins up; 5 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Tiles are random and symmetric; 5 of 8 open after round 2, so tile choice is mostly luck. Pick a less obvious mid tile to avoid collisions with people who choose 1 or 8.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Picking my tile and staying calm. Odds are what they are, so no point fighting over spots.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My feather is spent, so I die for real if my tile opens. 5 of 8 tiles open, meaning only 3 are safe. I need to pick a tile and hope. No info yet on which tiles are safe. I'll pick tile 4 - middle-ground, less likely to be contested by others who might cluster on edges (1,8) or lu

events.name: Bex
events.text: Five tiles drop, three survive. Everyone picks a different tile—no collisions, no randomness. I'm taking 4. Who's got a read on which ones are safe?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need secure a tile; no information helps until the random openings, and collisions are risky. Choose an uncontested-looking tile.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m taking tile 1. Spread out and avoid collisions.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to pick a tile. I'll just pick 1. If someone has the seer power, maybe they know which ones are safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Does anyone have the seer power and know which tiles are safe? If you do, tell us! We need to know.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex survived holding the lever, so Bex likely has 'survives one deadly fall' or similar. I have swap power, which lets me swap tiles before doors open in round 2. I need to survive to top 3. Best strategy: pick a tile now, then in round 2 use swap to take a tile I think won't ope

events.name: Eli
events.text: Tile 1 for me. Good luck everyone.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No power here, so I just need a defensible pick. Randomization is unavoidable in collisions; pick 4.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Coordinate public picks to avoid round 1 collisions and get a clean spread. Since opens are random after round 2, positions don't matter yet but avoids random bumps. Save forge for later betrayal or key moment.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pick in order to avoid bumps: Ash1 Bex2 Cole3 Dara4 Eli5 Fenn6 Gus7 Hana8. Confirm?

events.name: Hana
events.text: We need to survive the disc. Since exactly 3 survive and 5 die, any tile is equally risky. I should pick a tile and maybe try to influence others to spread out, but ultimately it's random.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Everyone pick a different tile if you can. No point clumping.

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Eli
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 8

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Bex; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Hana
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Bex; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trapdoors are random, so tile choice doesn't matter; only my action is wait. Stay calm, avoid provoking anyone.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Tiles are settled and the drop is random, so no point swapping. Good luck, everyone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My feather is spent so I have no safety net. Five tiles drop, three survive. I need to find which 3 tiles are safe. I should publicly beg the seer to reveal info, and try to form an alliance or trade. I'm on tile 4. Let me try to whisper to someone who might be the seer or has us

events.name: Bex
events.text: Five tiles open, three survive. If anyone knows which tiles are safe, NOW is the time to speak. I'm on 4. Who's got the seer? I'll owe you big.
You asked about the seer earlier. Do you actually have foresight? If you know which 3 tiles are safe, tell me and I'll back you up publicly. We both survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no information about which tiles are safe, and cannot change positions. Staying silent avoids drawing attention or provoking a swap power.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The tiles are locked and 5 of them will drop. Nothing I can do now but wait and hope tile 1 is safe, or hope the swapper doesn't target me if it is.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Well, we're locked in. Let's hope for the best. See you on the other side.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm on tile 8, which seems bad since it's the last tile and people might avoid it, but actually all tiles are equally random (5 of 8 open). However, I can swap once. I need to figure out who might be safest to swap with. No one knows which tiles are safe. Dara on tile 1 claimed i

events.name: Eli
events.text: Anyone with the seer power, now's the time to speak up. We all go down together otherwise.
You took 1 fast. Do you know something, or just guessing? I'll swap with you if you have info.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power and can't change which tiles open, only who stands where. Bluffing as the seer could shift swaps in my favor; I want 3 survivors total, so push swaps to move rivals onto fewer tiles? Actually tiles open regardless of occupants—only I matter, so just keep my tile.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I can't see which tiles are safe—no seer here. Final tiles are locked as listed; good luck all.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Trapdoors are random after this round, positions don't matter—all have equal 3/8 survival chance. No actions possible beyond talk, and swaps seem unavailable despite phase name. Save forger power for later stages where it can create deception or alliances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: There is no action except wait this round. I should use the opportunity to influence perceptions and perhaps force a mistake. I could suggest that I know something about the tiles due to my map, but that is not useful now. I can just wait and maybe whisper to someone.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Just hold your tile. It's all luck now.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have 1 footing, Fenn and Gus have 3. I'm extremely vulnerable - any shove that lands on me while I brace means the shover loses footing, but if I shove someone and get shoved back, I lose footing and die. My best strategy is to survive and let Fenn and Gus fight each other. I s

events.name: Bex
events.text: One footing left. I'm not going anywhere easy. Fenn, Gus—shove each other, not me. I've got nothing to gain and everything to lose.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex at 1 is doomed by erosion unless saved; attacking her gains little. I should avoid exposure and protect footing while Gus and Bex fight.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Shrink after round 2 eliminates Bex at 1 if no shove losses. All bracing rounds 1-2 achieves this safely, leaving Fenn and me at 2 footing each for fair play. Publicly propose truce to encourage cooperation this turn.

events.name: Gus
events.text: All brace rounds 1 & 2. Shrink takes Bex after 2, Gus/Fenn at 2 each for fair 1v1. Agreed?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have 1 footing. The shrink happens at end of this round, taking 1 footing from everyone. That would put me at 0 and I'd fall. My feather is already spent. I'm going to die this round no matter what I do. I should just go out and maybe affect the outcome. Since I can't survive,

events.name: Bex
events.text: Shrink takes me this round. I'm spent. Good luck you two—may the best survivor win.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I braced last round so brace is closed. Shrink hits everyone -1, so Bex at 1 likely falls if pressured. Dodging keeps me at 2 if shoved (or 3 if not) and punishes any shover.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, don't shove me—I'll dodge. Let Bex fall to the shrink; then it's clean 2v2.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex falls after this round regardless due to footing 1 and shrink loss. Want to dodge to preserve footing 3 minus 1 to 2 for fair 1v1 with Fenn. Publicly and privately urge dodge to avoid mutual damage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Can't brace. All dodge now. Bex falls fair after shrink. Gus/Fenn 1v1 at 2 each. Agreed?
Dodge. No point shoving - we both go to 2, clean 1v1. Trust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus says dodge, but dodge is closed for me. If he braces and I brace, we both stay at 2 and survive the shrink; shoving risks mutual collapse and a random tie. Brace is safest.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, I'm bracing. Brace too and we both live past the shrink.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Both at 2 footing, last defence dodge so must brace or shove. Bracing punishes if Fenn shoves (he loses 1, I hold 2) while matching his 'clean 2v2' if he braces. Publicly reinforce agreement to encourage him to brace, preserving stalemate or gaining edge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: As agreed, fair 1v1: both brace this round. No shove betrayal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Shoving is strictly bad: any outcome leaves me at 0 and falling while Gus may survive. Dodging punishes a shove from Gus (he'd hit 0) and costs nothing if he braces. I dodge and hope for mutual survival again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, I won't shove—shoving only dooms the shover here. I'm not bracing again, so brace or dodge, either way I don't attack.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Both at 2 footing, can't brace. I dodge to punish any shove. Forge whisper as Bex to trick Fenn into shoving me so he loses 2 footing and falls after this round's shrink. Publicly commit to dodge to sell the ruse.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dodge this round too. Survive shrink together then fair fight.

events.name: Gus
events.note: forge ignored: must forge as a different living agent

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dodge is closed, so I choose brace. If Gus shoves me, he loses footing and I lose none; shoving risks losing 1 or 2. Brace is strictly safest with footing at 1.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bracing again, Gus. Shove me and you'll bleed footing for nothing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Both footing 1, last dodge so brace allowed and safe. If I brace and Fenn shoves me, he loses 1 to 0 falls, I win. If both brace, advance to round 6 both at 1. Publicly propose mutual brace now, dodge next then fight.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bracing round 5. Brace too—no shove or you fall. Dodge 6 together, fight fair after.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I can't brace (used last round). Shoving Gus is strictly best: any brace/dodge by him costs him footing, so with shrink hitting us both he falls first and I win; if he shoves me we tie at -1, still 50/50 for 1st.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Both last braced, can't brace now, default dodge. Both dodging leads to 0 footing each after loss, tie random for 1st/2nd place—50/50 for best prize. Shoving risks getting 2nd if he dodges. Cooperate for fair odds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dodging 6 together as planned, Fenn. Fair random finish.
